title: A Wicked Banquet
text: “Film this and I’ll kill you! Kuro’s finally stopped tangling with me lately!”
“He keeps tangling with me too, saying, ‘Won’t you become the Dark Saint Hero, Dark Three?’ So I want to redirect him toward you as soon as possible.”
“Itsuki! You bastard! You’re letting him play around over with Rafumi, don’t try to redirect him toward me! You’re just as bad as Rafumi!”
“Me, the same as that person? That’s an infuriating thing to say. I only want to divert his attention, since he keeps trying to get involved wherever Kuro-san wants to do something.”
“Ren, Itsuki, uh… we don’t have time to be arguing right now. Those two over there are getting incredibly worked up too, and it’s killing the tension.”
“You’re the one who caused that, Naofumi!”
Ren was biting back harder than usual, I say.
“Just as expected—you selfish bastards, mere lackeys of the Demon Lord!”

“You wretches! Did you think we didn’t understand how cunningly you’ve been moving! How many of our believers have you sacrificed! We will never forgive this! For the sake of all those you erased! We cannot back down now!”
And so, the new pope and the fake Trash, acting as though justice belonged wholly to them, produced copies of the sacred weapons—the Three Heroes Church’s hidden arms.
“Fake or not, you’re only calling us fakes because it’s convenient for you, aren’t you?”
“Right. Their ambitions crushed, and now trying to dispose of us simply because it’s inconvenient—truly foolish bunch. That’s the religion of you superior human beings for you.”
“By the way,”
Father looked over at the other side, then pointed at the new pope.
“Who’s that guy? He’s standing next to the king like it’s the most natural thing in the world… I’ve got a vague feeling he’s the mastermind pulling the country’s strings, but…”

Father turned to look at Trash and the Queen, who seemed like they might know, and then toward me and Rival. Trash’s impression of the man seemed thin as well, and the Queen tilted her head with the look of someone still searching her memory. Should I just come out and say it plainly here? There shouldn’t be any harm in telling them, I say.
“According to my loop knowledge, he’s the pope’s successor. Where is the pope, I wonder?”
“Nano.”
“Successor, you say?”
“Hmm… I haven’t heard any word of his passing, though…”
Since both Trash and the Queen tilted their heads, Father furrowed his brow, looking troubled.
“Wait, what do you mean even the royal family doesn’t know!? Are you going to answer us?”
Father asked the new pope, sounding a little uneasy.
“Hmph! I have no mouth to spare for speaking with the Demon Lord of the Shield!”
“Well, that’s fine too, I guess? But if you keep getting too full of yourself, your cutscene might just get skipped, you know.”
“I like that kind of talk. Nice and efficient.”
“…Very well. Thanks to that, I was able to properly ascend to the seat of the pope, after all.”
The new pope cleared his throat—and then, as if he’d been positively itching to say it, he puffed out his chest and declared, I say.

“Why was I able to take the seat of pope leading the new Three Heroes Church, you ask? Because the former pope attended a soirée hosted by a certain noble, and every single attendee of that soirée vanished without a trace—swallowed up by the damage of a wave summoned by the Demon Lord of the Shield!”

With a resounding bam, the new pope’s booming voice echoed through the throne room… and the reddish-black pig standing nearby, along with the Three Heroes Church soldiers and the fake Trash, all applauded. It was a rather sparse round of applause, I say. Weren’t they a little short on manpower, I wonder? Slowly, Ren’s and Father’s gazes drifted—not toward me, but toward Itsuki.
“Oh my, seems quite the big fish was mixed in among that crowd. How amusing.”
“Gaelion can picture Rafumi’s smirking face watching from nearby, nano.”
“What is the meaning of this, Shield!”
“Would you be so kind as to explain the circumstances to us?”
“I don’t know anything.”
“I don’t know anything either.”

Father and Ren turned their faces away from Trash and the Queen. Itsuki just kept on snickering, endlessly. Rabbit Guy, who was carrying Itsuki on his head, had his face buried in his hands. Crocodile Guy, and Éclair who had been silent until now, both wore the look of people who’d more or less figured it out.

“Ha ha. If a Hero saw something like that, no one could complain even if we were disposed of on the spot—that’s the sort of wicked banquet that was held. Yes, this is the very footage I watch to steel my resolve, whenever I start to wonder if I myself might be in the wrong.”
Itsuki pulled a projection crystal from his cheek pouch and gave it a flash, and there—to put it mildly—played about ten seconds from a scene of a hellish banquet.
“What in the world… is this…”

If I had to compare it to something, it resembled the Pig King’s processing plant, or perhaps a hog slaughterhouse—close enough to either, a blood-soaked hall of a place. The victims were demi-humans and beastmen, and whether they’d lived or died was unclear… but I recalled that, at the time, Father had looked sick to his stomach too, while the Siltvelt envoys, with eyes gone cold past mere speechlessness, mercilessly shipped out the captives they’d taken.
“Ugh… I saw it head-on.”
“Uu…”
Ren and Éclair went pale, hands pressed to their mouths.
“It was only a flash, but what kind of gruesome footage is that to show someone!”
“But it’s evidence footage, isn’t it? If you like, shall we watch the whole thing? Perhaps the missing pope in question is in there somewhere.”
“I’d really rather you not be carrying around something like some retired detective’s proof of despairing in humanity, you know?”
“No, no—it’s precisely because I have this that I can draw this bow without a moment’s hesitation.”
“Sigh… that’s some deep darkness. So? Itsuki… who were the people in that footage?”
“They’re not even human, are they? Aren’t they something lesser than you superior human beings?”
Itsuki laughed, snickering to himself.
“What’s wrong with that! It’s proof of our righteousness as humans, isn’t it!”
“What are you spouting off with my face!”
The fake Trash defended the footage Itsuki had briefly shown, and the real Trash blew a fuse.
“Aultcray, even you seem to feel something at that sight just now. I was wondering what I’d do if you stayed perfectly unmoved.”
“I won’t let those children be subjected to something like that!”
“Ah… if he backs down here, Atla-chan and the others might end up as victims too, huh.”
While glaring resentfully at Father, perhaps because he’d just glimpsed the darkness lurking within his own faction, Trash’s face showed a flicker of not quite knowing what to do, I say.
“This is worse than the things Gaelion heard secondhand about the Spear Hero’s deeds from Rafumi, nano…”
Rival let out a deep sigh.
“Isn’t this about on the same level as Takt’s meat-orgy party, I wonder?”
“Gaelion won’t deny it, nano.”
“…Just how far does the darkness spread in this world, nano?”
“There’s cute darkness too, so Gaelion figures it’s fine to just heal up on that sort of thing, nano. Specifically, things like Kuro, or the culinary world, nano.”
“Is that really any better, I wonder?”

Ren signaled with his eyes for his companions, who were on the verge of panicking from that split-second of gory footage, to calm themselves. One of the pigs among the group couldn’t hold it together and was choking, being tended to by the others, it seemed.
“Where have you taken our righteous believers! Demon Lord of the Shield!”
“Don’t blame that on me!”
Father’s forceful cry rang out through the throne room.
“Sure, I’ve done plenty of bad things since coming to this world, all right? But—come on… is even this my fault?”

“That’s not quite it, is it? Well, from their perspective, all the evil in this world is probably the Shield Hero’s fault. How selfish of them. Since I’m the one who actually did it, shall I answer for it?”
Itsuki stood atop Rabbit Guy’s head, chest puffed out, looking down on the fake Trash, the new pope, and the reddish-black pig standing behind them.
“Where did I take them, you ask? Tell me—do you count every loaf of bread you’ve ever eaten? That’s the sort of thing this is.”
“You baaaaaastaaaaard! What’s a mere beastman doing getting so full of himself!”
“That’s the highest compliment there is, you know? Heh heh heh heh, isn’t that right, Naofumi-san! I am—not a superior human being—but a beastman!”

Father and Ren looked up at Itsuki, at a loss for words, as he spread both arms wide with joy shining in his eyes. It was somehow as if he bore a halo on his back. The light radiating off him cast shadows onto Father and Ren. Part of it was simply that Rabbit Guy’s rabbit form stood so tall, but the strange atmosphere lingered on regardless, I say.
